out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Parasite Destruction
violations.observation: The following fish offered for service or sale in the ready-to-eat form was not frozen to ensure parasite destruction: raw lime-marinated tilapia in ceviche.
violations.corrective_action: Before service or sale in ready-to-eat form, raw or partially cooked fish shall be: 1) frozen and stored at a temperature of -4F or below for a minimum of 7 days in a freezer, or 2) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -31F or below for a minimum of 15 hours, or 3) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -4F or below for a minimum of 24 hours. CDI: CFM agreed to discontinue using the uncooked lime- marinated tilapia in the ceviche until EHS is provided the parasite destruction letter from the supplier Prime Meats. CHILCANOS (Inspection Date: 10/19/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shelled eggs stored above RTE romaine lettuce inside the Kolpak walk in refrigerator in the main kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: CFM relocated raw shelled eggs to bottom shelf inside the Kolpak walk in refrigerator.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: containers diced tomatoes (45F) inside the Avantico 2 Dr preptop refrigerator on the front cookline area.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: CFM relocated container of diced tomatoes to the walk in refrigerator to properly cool to 41F or below

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: plastic squeeze bottles of sauces (oil, water, brown sauce) and plastic containers of dry seasonings and spices (sugar, salt, cayenne pepper, brown sugar, anise star, etc.) throughout the front and back cookline in the main kitchen.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Boxes and containers of food stored on the floor inside the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. CDI: CFM relocated the boxes and containers of food to the shelves inside the walk in refrigerator and freezer.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoop in container of standing water (67F) next to rice warmer on the front cookline and plastic scoop handles directly touching dry bulk food (salt, sugar) in the back main kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CDI: CFM discarded the standing water from the container, washed, rinsed, and sanitized the rice scoop and will keep dry in between use and relocated the plastic scoop handles up and out of the dry bulk food (sugar, salt) items.

out_items.name: Pasteurized eggs used where required

violations.title: Pasteurized eggs substituted for raw eggs in uncooked, egg-based recipes
violations.observation: Raw shell eggs are used in the preparation of the following ready-to-eat foods without subsequent full cooking: OBSERVED ON DRINK MENU: PISCO SOUR REGULAR WHICH CONTAINS EGG WHITE. PIC STATED SOMETIMES THEY USE RAW EGG WHITE, SOMETIMES PASTEURIZED EGG WHITE.
violations.corrective_action: Pasteurized eggs or egg products shall be substituted for raw eggs in the preparation of foods such as Caesar salad, hollandaise, or Bearnaise sauce, mayonnaise, meringue, eggnog, ice cream, and egg fortified beverages and recipes that where egg ingredient is not fully cooked and when the consumer is not informed by a disclosure and reminder statement. CDI: PIC AGREED TO CEASE MAKING DRINK WITH UNPASTEURIZED EGG WHITE UNTIL A CONSUMER ADVISORY IS ADDED TO DRINK MENU. PLEASE ADD A DISCLOSURE AND REMINDER STATEMENT AND AN ASTERISK NEXT TO THE STATEMENTS AND THE MENU ITEM IF YOU DO NOT CONSISTENTLY USE PASTEURIZED EGG WHITE. THE STATEMENT SHOULD READ AS FOLLOWS (OR USING A DIFFERENT VERSION FROM FAIRFAX COUNTY WEBSITE): “*MAY CONTAIN RAW OR UNDERCOOKED INGREDIENTS. CONSUMING RAW OR UNDERCOOKED MEATS, POULTRY, SEAFOOD, SHELLFISH, OR EGGS MAY INCREASE YOUR RISK OF FOODBORNE ILLNESS, ESPECIALLY IF YOU HAVE CERTAIN MEDICAL CONDITIONS.”

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken over raw beef.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). Order rearranged.
